name: Kerion Celsi

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and mycological diagnosis of Kerion Celsi

criteria.description: Presence of a boggy, inflammatory, tender scalp plaque with pustules and crusting
Isolation of dermatophyte fungi from scalp lesion by culture or microscopy
Tender regional lymphadenopathy adjacent to the scalp lesion
Localized hair loss with broken hairs in the affected area

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of inflammatory scalp lesion with positive fungal culture or microscopy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by mycological confirmation; biopsy rarely needed

laboratory: Positive direct microscopic examination of hair and scalp scrapings with KOH revealing fungal hyphae
Positive fungal culture identifying dermatophyte species (commonly Trichophyton or Microsporum)
Elevated inflammatory markers in some cases (e.g., ESR, CRP)
imaging: Ultrasound may show subcutaneous edema and abscess formation in severe cases
other: Histopathology showing intense inflammatory infiltrate with fungal elements in hair follicles (rarely performed)

distinguishingFeatures: Rapid onset with purulent abscess without fungal elements

redFlags: Rapidly expanding scalp lesion with systemic signs of infection
Failure to respond to antifungal therapy
Development of abscess or extensive scarring alopecia
references: Hay RJ, et al. Tinea capitis and kerion. In: Fitzpatrick's Dermatology in General Medicine. 9th ed. 2019.
Elewski BE. Tinea capitis: a current perspective. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2000;42(1 Pt 1):1-20.
